subject: SIG: Clarifications needed on KEK provenance, HSM egress, and rotation attestation
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Clarification on key provenance and HSM egress controls

Hi Ben —

We are working through the SIG and have a few follow-up items specific to encryption and key management that need clarification before our procurement loop closes. Can you please confirm/provide evidence for the following by COB PT Friday 27 Jun?

1) KEK provenance: are customer data-encrypting keys (DEKs) wrapped with a KEK generated inside an HSM (FIPS) or an AWS KMS key (HSM-backed)? Please state how KEKs are generated for (a) hosted Redwood API customers, (b) Dedicated/reserved deployments, and (c) Private/VPC/on-prem deployments.

2) Plaintext export policy: does Redwood ever export KEKs or DEKs in plaintext for any process (migration, support, emergency)? If exports are possible, describe the authorization path, controls, and audit trail.

3) Rotation cadence & evidence: what is the KEK rotation schedule/policy and where can we see rotation events? Provide a short timeline of the most recent rotation and redacted audit logs showing the operation (timestamps + initiating principal).

4) HSM egress & vendor controls: which HSM vendors are in use (if any)? Is there any scenario where keys or key material leaves the HSM boundary in cleartext? Please attach vendor FIPS/HSM factsheets or certs and your written attestation to the above statements.

We appreciate concrete artifacts (rotation tables, redacted logs, vendor factsheets, and a signed attestation). If anything requires legal/engineering signatures or a narrow SLA carve-out, please call that out.

Thanks —
Alice
Procurement / Security, Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarification on key provenance and HSM egress controls — evidence bundle

Ben / Alice — attaching the consolidated packet. Summary answers below and attachments are listed at the bottom. If Acme needs a signed PDF with the security org signature block we can provide it next business day; this email provides the operational answers and pointers to artifacts.

Summary answers (concise):
1) KEK provenance:
- Hosted (Redwood API): KEKs are AWS KMS CMKs (HSM-backed) created and owned by Redwood in our dedicated KMS accounts. We use AWS KMS multi-region keys for critical cross-region customers.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): KEKs can be either Redwood-managed KMS CMKs (same as hosted) or customer-managed KMS keys depending on the contract. We clearly document the choice in the provisioning checklist.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: customers may BYOK or BYOHSM; when BYOHSM is selected keys remain under the customer HSM control and Redwood does not receive unwrapped key material.

2) Plaintext export policy:
- Redwood does not export KEKs or DEKs in plaintext in any normal operational flow. Emergency export of key material in cleartext is not an allowed practice.
- In limited, documented DR scenarios where a customer has explicitly contracted an emergency key extraction process (rare, contract-level), the operation requires a multi-party authorization (Security + Customer PoC + Legal), recorded video of the key ceremony, and an immutable audit trail. We have not performed such an export for production customer keys in the last five years.

3) Rotation cadence & evidence:
- KEK rotation policy: default scheduled rotation every 12 months for KEKs; cryptographic material derived from KEKs (DEKs) may use shorter lifespans depending on workload. Emergency rotations are performed immediately after an incident and follow the rotation SOP.
- Evidence provided: attached redacted audit logs showing the rotation events (timestamps and RedactedPrincipalName), and an xlsx rotation timeline listing the last three scheduled rotations.

4) HSM vendor & egress:
- Vendor(s): Redwood uses AWS KMS (AWS-managed HSMs) for hosted flows. For customers electing BYOHSM we have validated integrations with HSM vendors including Thales Luna and Gemalto (see attached factsheets).
- Egress: keys do not leave HSMs in cleartext. HSMs and KMS provide cryptographic boundary protections; any key export capability is vendor-limited and requires split-authority/ceremony. We explicitly prohibit plaintext egress in our standard service terms.

Attachments included in packet:
- redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf (concise SIG Q&A & attestation draft)
- kek_rotation_timeline_q2-2025.xlsx (rotation table, redacted principals)
- hsm_vendor_factsheet_thales_luna.pdf (vendor factsheet & FIPS refs)
- audit_rotations_redacted.txt (redacted KMS audit lines showing rotation events)

Notes & follow-ups:
- If Acme requires the attestation signed by Head of InfoSec, please indicate the signer and we will route through legal for signature.
- If you want KMS ARNs or per-customer key identifiers, we can provide them under an NDA or within the procurement contract (we do not share production ARNs publicly).

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
